verdict: The Greek itself is mostly sound and often genuinely well observed – the imperfective/perfective pair at hs-0667, the pain-is-done-to-you frame at hs-0409, ΚΤΕΛ, θερμοσίφωνας, σκέτο/μέτριο/γλυκό, and every one of the N/A calls (no honorific particle, no side-marked kin, no ergative marker, no vector verbs) are correct – but as a shippable Greek syllabus this is not ready, for three reasons that all trace back to the Hindi spine. First, the scaffolding is still learner-facing: six notes contain Devanagari (हाथ, रसोई/किचन, प्रणाम, ने, जाना/लेना/देना, साला/देवर), about twenty more explain a Greek word by what it replaces in an Indian course (paneer, samosa, khichdi, raita, namkeen, cricket, rickshaws, garam masala, turmeric, pressure cooker, air-cooler, UPI, touching an elder's feet), a dozen say things like 'this slot carries' or 'replaces the app-cab slot', and five still open with 'Re-tiered up:'. A British learner of Greek reads none of that as help. Second, well over seventy rows repeat an earlier row, frequently with conflicting tiers (φακές 3 and 4, κόσμος 2 and 3, φορτιστής 2 and 3, παππούς 2 and 3, χίλια 2 and 3, κουζίνα three times, γίνομαι three times, μια χαρά three times), which will schedule the same card twice on two different intervals. Third, and worst, the absences are ones no Greek curriculum would produce: καλημέρα is nowhere in the list, surviving only inside another item's note, and neither are τρώω, πληρώνω, υπάρχει, χθες, κρασί, μπίρα, γύρος/σουβλάκι, ταβέρνα, θάλασσα, παραλία, νησί, πλατεία, λιμάνι, πλοίο, δίπλα σε, ρέστα, περίπτερο or φούρνος – while twelve month names sit at tier 4 and μπατζανάκης, ιδρώτας and κουβάς each hold a slot. There is also nothing anywhere on decoding the alphabet (μπ/ντ/γκ, ει/οι/η/υ) or on the stress accent, which for a Brit is the actual day-one obstacle, and the romanisation runs two incompatible schemes side by side (δωμάτιο is 'dhomátio' at hs-0168 and 'domátio' at hs-0904; χ appears as h, kh and ch; hs-0300 has a Greek α sitting inside the roman field). Do the note sweep, dedupe, add the fifty items above and settle on one romanisation, and this becomes a strong list; ship it as it stands and the first thing the learner meets is a Greek course that greets them in Devanagari and cannot say good morning.

«με λεμόνι» – squeezed over fish, meat, chips, everything

Said to anyone about to eat, including strangers at the next table

τηγάνι = frying pan; γάστρα is the covered dish for oven-baked meat

«με θέα στη θάλασσα» = with a sea view – worth asking for
ταβάνι = ceiling; στέγη = a pitched roof
όροφος is a storey: «τρίτος όροφος» = third floor
«Πύλη 12»; a garden gate is a καγκελόπορτα
κλειδώνω = to lock; «Κλείδωσες;»

τζάμι = the glass in a window; γυαλί = glass the material
φλιτζάνι is a cup with a saucer

οδοντόκρεμα = toothpaste
The big street bins; a kitchen bin is a σκουπιδοτενεκές

items.en: to turn on (a light); to light
